title: A specified splitting of the punctured active-root colimit descends
statement: Let $B,A$ be commutative rings with $A$ a $B$-algebra, $r,s\geq0$, $t:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to B$, $\alpha:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, and $p\in\mathbf N$. Put $f=\prod_i t_i$, $T_m=A[z_j]/(z_j^m-t_{\alpha(j)})$, $Q_m=T_m[1/f]$, and $Q_\infty=\varinjlim_{(m,p)=1}Q_m$ with the canonical root power transitions [def-sfb-active-root-normalization-pushout-data]. Let $D$ be a finitely presented $B[1/f]$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For $d\geq0$, let $\theta:D\otimes_{B[1/f]}Q_\infty\simeq Q_\infty^d$ be a specified $Q_\infty$-algebra isomorphism. There exist $m>0$ coprime to $p$ and a $Q_m$-algebra isomorphism $\theta_m:D\otimes_{B[1/f]}Q_m\simeq Q_m^d$ such that for every $x\in D$ and $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)$, the image in $Q_\infty$ of $\theta_m(x\otimes1)_j$ equals $\theta(x\otimes1)_j$. No characteristic, normality or geometric-point assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras (2),(3), and affine Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation; parent steps 1--3.

proof.text: The prime-to-$p$ positive integers ordered by divisibility form a directed set with initial element $1$: $ab$ is a common upper bound of $a,b$. At level $1$, $Q_1=A[1/f]$. Put $H_m=D\otimes_{B[1/f]}Q_m$. The assumed finite presentation of D gives one for its base change. Substituting the coefficient map into its finitely many defining polynomials gives a finite presentation of $H_1$ over $Q_1$, and of $H_m=H_1\otimes_{Q_1}Q_m$. Also $Q_1^d$ is finitely presented: use generators $e_1,\ldots,e_d$, relations $e_i^2=e_i$, $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, and $\sum e_i=1$. This presentation is a product because every polynomial reduces uniquely to $\sum a_ie_i$, with $a_i$ its value at the $i$-th coordinate vector. For $d=0$ the sole relation is $1=0$.

Apply the morphism clause (2) of the cited algebra-colimit theorem over the directed system $Q_m$, first to $\theta_\infty:H_\infty\to Q_\infty^d$, and then to its inverse. Both source and target are the base changes of the finitely presented $Q_1$-algebras in Step 1. Identify scalar extension of a finite product by the mutually inverse formulas $(a_i)\otimes q\mapsto(a_iq)_i$ and $(q_i)_i\mapsto\sum e_i\otimes q_i$. This includes the empty product. Take a common upper bound of the two resulting indices and denote the descended maps there by $u:H_a\to Q_a^d$ and $w:Q_a^d\to H_a$. Their scalar extensions are the given maps, rather than merely some splitting and its inverse.

The composites $wu$ and $uw$ extend to the identities over $Q_\infty$. Apply equality clause (3) of the same theorem to each composite and its identity, and take a common upper bound $m$ of the two indices. The maps at level $m$ are inverse. Thus $\theta_m=u_m$ is an isomorphism with scalar extension exactly $\theta_\infty$. No injection of $Q_a\to Q_\infty$ is used: eventual equality is precisely the supplied clause (3).
